source_text:
Ἐπεὶ δε ποτε κατέπαυσεν τὴν προσευχήν, μνημονεύσας ἁπάντων καὶ τῶν πώποτε συμβεβληκότων αὐτῷ, μικρῶν τε καὶ μεγάλων, ἐνδόξων τε καὶ ἀδόξων καὶ πάσης τῆς κατὰ τὴν οἰκουμένην καθολικῆς ἐκκλησίας, τῆς ὥρας ἐλθούσης τοῦ ἐξιέναι, ὄνῳ καθίσαντες αὐτὸν ἤγαγον εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ὄντος σαββάτου μεγάλου.
καὶ ὑπήντα αὐτῷ ὁ εἰρήναρχος Ἡρώδης καὶ ὁ πατὴρ αὐτοῦ Νικήτης, οἳ καὶ μεταθέντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὴν καροῦχαν ἔπειθον παρακαθεζόμενοι καὶ λέγοντες: Τί γὰρ κακόν ἐστιν εἰπεῖν: Κύριος καῖσαρ, καὶ ἐπιθῦσαι καὶ τὰ τούτοις ἀκόλουθα καὶ διασώζεσθαι; ὁ δὲ τὰ μὲν πρῶτα οὐκ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς, ἐπιμενόντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἔφη: Οὐ μέλλω ποιεῖν, ὃ συμβουλεύετέ μοι.
οἱ δὲ ἀποτυχόντες τοῦ πεῖσαι αὐτὸν δεινὰ ῥήματα ἔλεγον αὐτῷ καὶ μετὰ σπουδῆς καθῄρουν αὐτόν, ὡς κατιόντα ἀπὸ τῆς καρούχας ἀποσῦραι τὸ ἀντικνήμιον. καὶ μὴ ἐπιστραφείς, ὡς οὐδὲν πεπονθὼς προθύμως μετὰ σπουδῆς ἐπορεύετο, ἀγόμενος εἰς τὸ στάδιον, θορύβου τηλικούτου ὄντος ἐν τῷ σταδίῳ, ὡς μηδὲ ἀκουσθῆναί τινα δύνασθαι.
thought_title: Polycarp's arrest and journey to the stadium
orientation: Polycarp has just finished a long prayer after learning he is to be arrested, and now the police captain Herod and his father Nicetes take him into the city.
pass_a_gloss: And when he had finished the prayer, having remembered all and those who had ever met with him, small and great, famous and obscure, and all the catholic church throughout the inhabited world, when the hour came to depart, having seated him on a donkey they led him into the city, it being a great Sabbath. And the police captain Herod met him and his father Nicetes, who also having transferred him onto the carriage were persuading him, sitting beside him and saying: For what harm is it to say: Lord Caesar, and to sacrifice and the things that follow these and to be saved? But he at first did not answer them, and when they persisted he said: I am not going to do what you advise me. And they, having failed to persuade him, spoke terrible words to him and with haste pulled him down, so that as he was getting down from the carriage he scraped his shin. And not turning around, as if having suffered nothing, eagerly with haste he went on, being led into the stadium, there being such a great uproar in the stadium that no one could even be heard.

Glossary term for the local official responsible for public order.

Preserves the passive voice and the sense of escaping death by compliance.

pass_b_english: When he had finished his prayer, he had remembered everyone who had ever crossed his path, small and great, honored and obscure, and the whole catholic church throughout the world, the hour came for him to leave. They seated him on a donkey and brought him into the city. It was a great Sabbath.

The police captain Herod met him, along with Herod's father Nicetes. They moved him into their carriage, sat beside him, and tried to persuade him. "What harm is there," they said, "in saying, 'Lord Caesar,' and sacrificing and doing the rest that follows, and so saving yourself?" At first he gave them no answer. But when they kept pressing him, he said, "I am not going to do what you advise me."

When they failed to persuade him, they spoke harsh words to him and pulled him down with such haste that, as he got out of the carriage, he skinned his shin. But he did not turn back. As if nothing had happened to him, he walked on eagerly and quickly, led into the stadium. The uproar there was so great that no one could even be heard.

problems.why: καροῦχα is a sedan chair/litter, not a wheeled carriage.
problems.ruling: καροῦχα denotes a sedan chair/litter, not a wheeled carriage; 'their carriage' misleads readers about the vehicle type.

problems.why: ἀντικνήμιον is the shin/calf, but ἀποσῦραι means 'to tear away/skin,' not merely scrape.
problems.ruling: ἀποσῦραι means 'tear away/skin/strip,' stronger than 'scraped'; 'scraped' understates the violence of ἀποσῦραι τὸ ἀντικνήμιον.
